title.narrative: SALAR/SKL - Stöd för inkluderande och ansvarsfull styrning (AGIR) i DRC
SALAR/SKL - Support for Inclusive and Accountable Governance (AGIR) in the DRC

description.narrative:
SKL International is the extended operational arm of SALAR in international development cooperation with a wide range of experiences in supporting decentralisation and local government reforms globally. As an integral and fully owned company of SALAR it seeks to promote sustainable systems of local self-government, areas that Sida wishes to strengthen in DRC and aligned to priorities of the Swedish development cooperation in DRC.
The project, entitled Appui à la Gouvernance Inclusive et Redevable (AGIR), works towards Increased access to and quality of public services and participation in decision making for women, men, boys and girls, and marginalised groups through tailored governance interventions in selected ETDs and working on improved interactions on provincial level between various governance stakeholders. AGIR will aim to promote changes in actions, practices, behaviours, relationships and processes of targeted actors.

Detta projektförslag har tagits fram genom en förstudie på uppdrag av Svenska ambassaden i Kinshasa till Sveriges Kommuner och Landsting (SKL). Förstudien engagerade cirka 55 nyckelintressenter (lokala, provinsiella, nationella och internationella) för att analysera den möjliggörande miljön för lokalt självstyre, kapaciteten, begränsningarna och behoven hos lokala myndigheter (Entités Territoriales Decentralisés, ETDs) samt tillagda värde gentemot andra insatser. Förstudien drog slutsatsen att stödjande ETD är den mest relevanta startpunkten för ett SALAR/SKL Internationellt projektintervention. Det finns mer än 1400 ETD:er i Demokratiska republiken Kongo, med konstitutionellt sett ganska omfattande uppgifter för att stärka det sociala kontraktet med medborgarna. ETD:er ska enligt lagen tillhandahålla ett antal viktiga tjänster till medborgarna, inklusive byggande, utveckling och underhåll av lokala vägar, organisation av offentliga marknader, lokala polistjänster, hygien, sanitet och avlopp, underhåll av offentliga byggnader, konstruktion och rehabilitering av daghem centrum och skolor, allmän belysning, räddningstjänst, etablering av sociala och kulturella centrum m.m. Det faktiska tillhandahållandet av tjänster är dock obefintligt eller otillräckligt inom de flesta av dessa områden. Genomförandet av decentraliseringsprocessen har gjort minst framsteg på lokal nivå: ETD:er har mycket begränsad tillgång till resurser, möter legitimitetsutmaningar (eftersom lokala val inte har hållits) och har litet inflytande i beslutsfattandet på decentraliseringsprocessen. Samtidigt är ETD:er den regeringsnivå som ligger närmast befolkningen. Därför kan projektet, genom att stödja effektivare, transparenta och inkluderande styrningsformer på denna nivå, bidra till starkare ansvarsförhållanden genom att skapa närmare band mellan medborgare och beslutsfattare, och därigenom mildra demokratiklyftan i frånvaron av valda lokala församlingar.

This project proposal was developed through a Pre-Study commissioned by the Swedish Embassy in Kinshasa to the Swedish Association of Local Authorities and Regions (SALAR). The Pre-Study engaged about 55 key stakeholders (local, provincial, national and international) to analyse the enabling environment for local self-governance, the capacity, constraints and needs of local government units (Entités Territoriales Decentralisées, ETDs) as well as added value vis-à-vis other interventions. The Pre-Study concluded that supporting ETDs is the most relevant entry-point for a SALAR/SKL International project intervention. There are more than 1400 ETDs in the DRC, with constitutionally quite wide-ranging tasks in strengthening the social contract with citizens. ETDs should according to the law provide a number of essential services to citizens, including construction, development and maintenance of local roads, organisation of public markets, local police services, hygiene, sanitation and sewage, maintaining public buildings, construction and rehabilitation of day care centres and schools, public lighting, emergency services, establishment of social and cultural centres, etc. However, actual service provision is inexistant or insufficient in most of those areas. Implementation of the decentralisation process has advanced the least on the local level: ETDs have very limited access to resources, face legitimacy challenges (as local elections have not been held) and have little influence in decision making on the decentralisation process. At the same time, ETDs are the tier of government closest to the population. Therefore, by supporting more effective, transparent and inclusive forms of governance at this level, the project can contribute to stronger relationships of accountability by creating closer ties between citizens and decision makers, thereby mitigating the democracy gap in the absence of elected local assemblies.

sector.narrative: Decentralisation and support to subnational government

description.narrative:
This Annual report constitutes the second annual report for the project AGIR, "Appui a la gouvernance inclusive et redevable", lasting from July 2022 to August 2027 and It reports on the results of the second year of the project, d'août 2023 à juillet 2024, from August 2023 through July 2024. The project has seen progress in fostering decentralisation, institutional support, and improving public service delivery in the six partner ETDs (Territorial Decentralised Entities) of: Likasi, Kikula, Katuba, Lubumbashi, Kasumbalesa, and Balamba as well as the Provincial Decentralisation division.
Throughout the second year, AGIR focused on strengthening the governance framework and supporting ETD institutions in key areas. Major activities included: Capacity building workshops: A series of workshops was organised for ETD staff and newly elected local council members covering decentralisation principles, gender-responsive governance, and public financial management, helping clarify roles and responsibilities. Economic and Perception Studies: Comprehensive studies on financial capacity and citizen perceptions of public services were conducted in all six ETDs. These studies provided a solid baseline for the project's interventions, identifying governance gaps and improvement areas. Operational support and tools development: The project assisted ETDs in developing practical planning tools including Local Development Plans (PLD) and Annual Investment Plans (PAI). Formal launch and partnerships: AGIR hosted an official launch event in Lubumbashi, engaging national, provincial, and local authorities. Memorandums of Understanding were signed with all partner ETDs, formalising partnerships and solidifying AGIR's supporting role.
The following key achievements can be noted for the respective outcome areas:
Outcome 1: Improved Local Governance (Efficiency, Transparency, Accountability, Coordination) Clarification of roles and responsibilities: AGIR clarified governance roles within the six partner ETDs, reducing conflicts and enhancing collaboration between departments. Conflict resolution and inter-department collaboration: AGIR mediated cooperation between local departments, improving resource sharing and removing illegal barriers to trade. Planning and budgeting improvements: Targeted ETDs made progress in planning, with their PIAs initiating projects concretely benefiting the local population. Revenue mobilisation: Significant strides were made in tax collection e.g. by reactivating dormant taxes in targeted ETDs.
Outcome 2: Enhanced Public Services Citizen engagement: AGIR reactivated Development Committees (CLDs and CDQs), encouraging greater citizen participation in governance. Service improvements: Based on studies and dialogue with the ETDs, concrete actions have been identified that can deliver tangible public service benefits. Strengthening civil registration: AGIR has engaged specifically to support civil registration services with the aim to enhance social protection, particularly for women and children. Gender inclusion: Specific progress was made in gender-responsive governance, with women participating in budget planning meetings for the first time.
Outcome 3: Strengthened Provincial Cooperation Improved dialogue: AGIR facilitated stronger interactions between ETDs and provincial authorities, ensuring alignment with national decentralisation strategies. Inter-ETD collaboration: AGIR has initiated facilitation of inter-ETD partnerships in relevant service delivery areas Advocacy: Partner ETDs have been supported to advocate e.g. to take local control over revenues, ensuring critical funding for community projects.
The project has worked consciously to integrate cross-cutting perspectives in different ways. Poverty reduction efforts support revenue mobilisation and encourage public participation in local governance to strengthen service delivery. Sustainability is pursued by fortifying existing structures, fostering partnerships, and encouraging stakeholder collaboration to improve service quality without
dependency. Environmental priorities include waste management and resilient agriculture, while gender equality initiatives aim to increase awareness, bolster ETD gender units, and improve civil registration to protect social and financial rights. Conflict sensitivity guides conflict resolution, and anti-corruption principles are emphasised via transparency, fostering trust within governance structures to ensure responsible resource use.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
